reason: (1) Ill-posed split: reg(Sym^m E) is a regularity over the algebraic closure of F_{p^n}, in the m e-coordinates. Lever 1 needs d_F of the Weil-restricted system in n*m (or l*m) F_q-coordinates. Weil restriction does not commute with regularity: the restricted ideal is a different ideal in a different ring. So 'reg(Sym^m E) is field- and n-independent' tells us nothing about the curve part after descent. (2) Additivity is false in general. The only known sum bound, reg(I+J) <= reg(I)+reg(J)-1 (Caviglia; Eisenbud-Huneke-Ulrich), needs Tor_{i>0}(R/I,R/J)=0, i.e. dim(I+J)=dim I+dim J-dim R. The descent system is zero-dimensional with about 2^{ml-n} points, built so the cover meets the subspace non-transversally (fibres split completely on the factor-base locus, per the monodromy closure). Tor-independence therefore fails exactly where the bound would be needed. Without it no additive or subadditive identity holds, and the residual is uncontrolled. (3) Even if it held, it would give an upper bound d_F <= f(m)+reg(subspace system). The subspace-only system is linear plus field equations, so its regularity is about l(q-1) for binary, which grows with l~n/m. A lower-bound route cannot come from an inequality that runs the other way. (4) d_F (last fall degree / max F4 degree) is not Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of a homogeneous ideal. It depends on the presentation, as the closures show for PKM towers. Comparing it with reg sums mixes invariants. (5) Nongenericity: this is accounting. It works on the polynomial system and changes no exponent and no B*D^2 vs N position. It is not CGK-generic, but it adds no cost reduction either. (6) Falsifier is weak: at n=7..13, d_F <= k+2 is already certified small (5-ish), so a residual of 0 or 1 is expected for trivial reasons and cannot separate the hypotheses (the card itself notes this risk). No computation was run, because the regularities in the formula do not live in the same ring, so the comparison is not well-defined.
